utterances.text: Later on, when you moved to Zenica, you socialised with people from Vitez. You must have heard stories. Did you hear anything about various kinds of units existing in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that there were Jokers in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and Vitezovi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Will you please answer with "Yes" or "No" to these questions? Did you hear that those Jokers were part of the military police?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know under whose command they were, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If you think it is absolutely essential, you may add something. Did you hear that there was a unit called Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that those Vitezovi were also called the HOS, H-O-S?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were called HOS, but I know that there were some HOS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you know that those units were the ones who wore black uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Units that were not HVO wore those other uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: When you use the term "HVO units," do you include any units belonging to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I personally believe that they all worked under the same command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But is it true that there were several different units?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know. This is just an assumption of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Tell us, you said that your late husband, Mr. Saban Mahmutovic, was an inspector in the municipality before the war, a police inspector?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, he was in the personnel service, in the cadaster of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: After the elections, when the HDZ and SDA shared positions in the municipality, then your husband, as a part of that agreement, became head of the police station?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: As part of the agreement between the HDZ and the SDA, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So he didn't have any policing experience?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The same applies to Pero Skopljak, his superior?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So both of them were appointed to those positions on political grounds?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned the event with the removal and hoisting of another flag in front of the police station. Do you know which flag was hoisted on the police station until that incident?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. I never even noticed whether there were any flags on any buildings or not. But when suddenly you see a chequerboard flag, then it becomes very conspicuous. Probably before that there was the usual flag flown at any police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina had any official flag in those days?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I believe it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity at any time, anywhere, to see the lily, the flag with the lilies?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Up until that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Which people considered that flag to be theirs? Which people were attached to that flag?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: In the beginning it was supposed to be a joint flag, but in the end it belonged to the Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So the Croats identified themselves with the other flag that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The Serbs, did they have the same flag?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The Serbs in Vitez did not have their own flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What about the Serbs in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I know the situation in Vitez, that the Croats and the Bosnians had their own flags. And as for the Serbs, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So each to his own. To still talk about the incident at the police station, who prevented the police officers from entering the building? Who prevented them from carrying on with their duties?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: My husband went, and on the way to work, he met Edib Zlotrg. They entered the station together. They were in the station -- this is what my husband told me. The national structure in the station favoured the Croats, the Croat police officers. They were the majority. The police officers who were also on sick leave were also there. My husband went to climb the stairs to go to his office. A police officer said, "You can't go upstairs." I remember that he said that he had said, "Are you the boss here, or am I?" And then he passed him by and went to his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In the end, they were driven out of the station?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were, at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, when your husband told you about this incident, did he mention anything about other people in other uniforms being present there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that before that, and I also heard that from what my husband had said to his friends, also from colleagues, from people in power. I had heard that people had arrived there, they were called Hercegovci. I don't know what they were doing there. They were brought there. They were mostly Croats who were brought there who were appointed to be the police officers there, and they were led by Pero Skopljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about two or three police officers who were working as uniformed police officers up until that time in the station when the situation calmed down a little bit, when they started talks, did they work for a while in that station, which was now under the control of the Croats?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: You mean Bosniak police officers?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. These were newly appointed police officers who were not working before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So there were some Bosniaks appointed there who were now working there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because the ones who worked there previously had left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So this situation didn't last too long; maybe a couple of weeks?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you hear, what were the reasons that they left?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not hear what their reasons for leaving were. The conflict broke out quickly, and probably that's why they left. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps hear from your husband that those police officers resigned with the explanation that they were threatened by members of their own community, the Muslim community?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I don't remember that. These were young people, perhaps two or three people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you didn't hear their reasons?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The attempts that were made to form a joint police force, so the Bosniaks in the police force were asked to sign some kind of statement, you mentioned that. So could you please tell us if you had ever exactly heard what this was about. Did somebody present them with a statement that they were supposed to sign, or was this something that was discussed at a meeting? What is this exactly about?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: At the meeting, when they came expecting that there would be a joint police force, they were told, "You have to leave MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina and join the MUP of Herceg-Bosna so that you can work together with us at the police station," which is something that they did not accept. They were told this by chief Samir, who told them that at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So this same approach, then, does that mean that they were given some kind of document about their jobs?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, this only happened at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did they ever receive some kind of paper or document that they were supposed to sign?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if there was any kind of document involved. I know that these were talks, and since they did not accept the terms, they could not enter the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You know about all of this from what your husband told you?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, and from what my colleagues told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So from other people?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So until the conflict broke out, there were two police stations?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: One in Stari Vitez, one in Vitez; one under the control of Croats, the other under the control of Muslims. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the citizens, too, in case of need, would go to, quote, their own police stations?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If somebody robbed a house, they would go and report that to a Croat house (sic), if they happened to be a Croat?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And the same would happen on the other side?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So there was a kind of dual role. Did you know that at that time, the armies also had their own military police?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember anything that had to do with the army. Probably the same situation was there as in the police, but I can't really tell you anything exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: At the time while we had at least two police stations in Vitez, perhaps possibly also military police, you had a television, had television broadcasts?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we had Croatian television, Vitez television.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you have any other TV stations?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we had the B and H television.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So it was the Republican television, and then the local station was from Vitez; could you receive Zetel?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what kind of newspapers would come to Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please pause between answer and question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, you're being asked to pause by the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Based on that information, did you have some kind of idea about the relations between Muslims and Croats in other municipalities outside of your town?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Generally the situation was the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: For example, at the end of '92, did you hear that there was a fierce conflict between the HVO and the B and H army in Novi Travnik, for example, which is a neighbouring municipality?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You told us that at the time, there were different incidents at that time, that explosive devices were planted in Muslim-owned stores, also in your house, near your house. Did this happen to the property of the Croats as well?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, this happened only to Bosniak property. Very rarely would it happen to a Croat, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Considering that the terms are "mostly" or "rarely," could you please answer with "yes" or "no": Did it happen to everybody?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, not to everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So to nobody, or just only to Muslims?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: If you -- would you like a concrete answer? It would happen more often to Muslims and very rarely to Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So more frequently, this would happen to Bosniaks than to Croats?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think we're being assisted by this. The witness has given her answer, so perhaps you would move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to be sure that I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: At the time when these explosions were being planted, did you hear that the restaurant Kamen (phoen) was blown up, and this was not far -- the restaurant was not far from Kolonija?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't individually remember. I know that the majority of the facilities were Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You told us that an explosive device was planted near your house. Could you please tell us what your neighbours were, houses that were close to you, to the left, to the right, behind you, across from you?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Left, to the left was Vahid's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: He was a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, a Muslim. Behind us was Fahrah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What was the name again?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Fahrah. In front of us was Fikreta. Pudza's house also was nearby, but it was more towards Fikret's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: To the left, or to the right?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: To the left. And to the left there was a man called Bagara. He was a Croat; I can't remember the first name of that man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So out of the four houses immediately close to your house, two were Muslim and two were Croat?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it could be two and two. Pudza's was half/half.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The bomb that was planted was planted in such a way that it was clear that it was targeting your house?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The bomb went off so loudly that we had the impression in the house that it was thrown at our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Later you saw where the bomb was planted?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the police came out later, but the police from Stari Vitez came out to see. I don't know what they found. The only thing I remember is that we had heard a powerful explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So police from Stari Vitez, we could call it Bosniak police, that came to the part of Vitez that was not under their control to do the investigation?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether the bomb exploded in your front yard, on the street, close to the street?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I can tell you nothing precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So nothing precisely; just that it was close?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, very close, and that it had exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Was there a fence around your house?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Was it inside, or outside the house?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, you didn't state very clearly what the damage to the house was.

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: There was no damage to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did the windows shatter?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, the windows did not shatter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So there was a strong explosion and a lot of fear?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was a strong explosion, and we were afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Concerning the same events, you said that Mrs. Besa -- you gave us her nickname --

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Besima.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: -- Besima, that she had received a telephone call which was a threatening call. Did you hear that conversation? Were you standing next to the telephone?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So she conveyed it to you?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was at work; my husband was also at work. She was alone in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So she told you when you came home?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, she called my husband to tell him about the call that she had received.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if she had said -- if the person had said where he was calling from?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Was she able to tell you anything about the accent, the tone of voice, something that could identify the caller?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Besa had been there for a few months, three or four months. She didn't know anybody, so she was not in a position to identify anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that your husband was a police officer, do you know if he had tried to question her about the details which could possibly lead to the identification of the caller?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he did try, but I don't remember that he established anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, could you please tell us where Besa worked?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Besa did not work. She was a refugee from Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What about you at that time?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: At that time I was working in Princip.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mrs. Mahmutovic, before the war, did you know Darko Kraljevic, who you mentioned a little earlier on in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know him in any special way. Vitez is a small town; we simply knew one another. I didn't know him in any particular way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, since you were in small town, did you know anything about the relations between Kraljevic and Mario Cerkez before the war?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: During the war?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: During the war? I just knew that they had come to my door together, but what they did, what they did together -- it's my impression, the impression of all of us from Vitez was that they were all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In the cafes that we mentioned, 072 and Benz, when you were living with the lady in Kolonija, did you ever see Darko Kraljevic there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, not directly. I was in a situation that I was not really able to look. I was too crazed by everything. But there were people there, and from conversations with Snjezana and all the people who would come to the house, it was obvious that there were different formations there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So this is how you heard?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and looking out from the window, I could see that these were people in different uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that Darko Kraljevic spent time there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, these were tales. These were stories.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you did hear about that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You said in response to questions from the Prosecutor regarding the visit of Kraljevic and Cerkez to your husband in the evening in January or February, you said, you said something like, "So far, I did not give such a statement." Would you please permit me to ask, you also talked about that in response to a question by my learned colleague Mr. Naumovski. You did give a statement when you came from Vitez to Zenica, you said that you gave a statement to police officers?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if that statement was written down?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I did not sign that statement, but it was probably taken down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Nobody offered you anything to sign?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, I simply explained -- told those people what had happened to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But you believe that this was taken down?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe that it should have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I ask a question? The Prosecutor this morning had, in his hands, a statement which was, by the way of its copying, similar to the statements we received through the discovery, statements of the various witnesses given in Zenica at that time. It was the set of the copies. More or less, they are, by appearance, very similar. I know that the Prosecutor was talking about Mr. Zlotrg, who also gave such a statement, but could the Prosecutor tell us whether he had a statement which the witness just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You want to know if there's another statement other than those that have been disclosed to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm asking that on the basis of what we mentioned this morning, that the first part of the statement is new here. I'm not sure that it's really new.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Lopez-Terres, have you got any other statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation) The Office of the Prosecutor has no other statement from Mrs. Mahmutovic. The only one we have is the one taken on the 3rd and 4th of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There are you, Mr. Kovacic. That's the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Okay. If they're done, they're done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: After those conversations in March '93, when you came from Vitez, you had no other conversations with any formal or informal bodies, other than talking with the Prosecutor and the investigators in March of that year?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Generally, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: May I ask what that "generally" means?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they were representatives from the Bosniak side who wanted to write a book. They would ask for photographs of my husband, so there were some conversations at that time, but it was nothing official. No documents were signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So it wasn't a formal interrogation, questioning?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So not the committee for investigating war crimes?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. During the visit of Cerkez and Kraljevic, to go back to that, the part of the conversation that you were present, that Cerkez, as far as I understood, was kind to you, that statement that he gave, and please correct me if I am wrong, he told you what he did for the purpose of calming you down?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did he calm you down?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't think that it would be anything so terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you didn't really think the situation was that dangerous?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I just heard loud noise, loud talk, and I came out to see what was happening. Then Cerkez told me, "Mrs. Mahmutovic, there are no problems, everything is okay." And I said, "Well, you're not going to do anything to my husband, you're not going to kill him," something to that effect. I said it as a joke. Then he answered, "Well, Mrs. Mahmutovic, there is no problem." So I went back into the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you were not particularly disturbed, frightened, and he also convinced you that there was no reason for you to feel like that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the reason I went out was the noise, their conversation. I was afraid that some incident may erupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear. Thank you. So during the part of the conversation during which you were present, or from what your husband said, did you gain any kind of impression about the relationship between Kraljevic and Cerkez? In which context were the two of them together there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Nothing; okay. Thank you. You mentioned that you had the impression that Cerkez was slightly intoxicated. Since you actually talked to him, could you confirm this or not?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I only came out for a moment, but when my husband came back, I asked him, "Why are you talking so loudly?" He told me that both of them had had something to drink.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But you didn't notice that yourself?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I only came out for a minute and then went back inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. You said that on the 15th of April, '93, your husband went to the fire station hall for the celebration. This was the celebration of the anniversary of the foundation of the army of B and H; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Are you sure that that was on the 15th, or was that the day before, on the 14th? Can you say decisively that this was on that date?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, the evidence has been, as I recollect, that there was such a party on the 15th. That was the undisputed evidence before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am afraid that there are some witnesses which -- and I'm not able to tell you now exactly, but I'm certain there are witnesses who said, "Well, it might have been on 14 or 15." At least two of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Mrs. Mahmutovic, do you remember, was it the 14th or the 15th?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Mahmutovic, could you please tell us if your late husband had told you anything directly before the outbreak of the conflict, so possibly on the 15th, that there had been a meeting in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The meeting that encouraged him, where he became optimistic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I know it's very difficult to remember, but you can answer with, "I know," or, "I don't know." Talking about this optimism, was that the result of this meeting at the municipal office or the result of the anniversary celebration at the fire station?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So this was on the basis of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, based on the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Of this meeting in the municipality or the one in the fire station?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't say exactly whether this happened in the municipality, but basically he was an optimist, based on the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You're sure this was the agreement of the 15th?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you can be sure of that directly, immediately the day before the attack?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not sure if this was quite clear to the others. The two of us know. You had heard that there was a meeting at the municipality on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I know only that on the 15th, my husband came, and he said, "Everything is all right. There will be no problems."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did he mention a meeting?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: "We had a joint meeting, and everything is okay. It's been agreed."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So from what he said, it was obvious that the meeting had taken place that day?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know why you're insisting on that day, but mainly he was happy with the outcome of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Talking about the first days of the conflict, the 16th of April, you mentioned that there was apparently an organised group that had been sent to your house?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The soldiers that came to your house which you told us about, you said that some of them had black uniforms and some of them had camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: It was mostly HVO uniforms. There was maybe one or two soldiers, I can't remember exactly, who had black uniforms, but mostly they had HVO uniforms with HVO insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So the HVO uniforms, according to you, are the camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the multi-coloured uniforms with the insignia of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you see those uniforms and the insignia?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: They were together with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: With the insignia of the HVO, did you see any kind of insignia indicating which units they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The name?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the HVO insignia and the checkerboard symbol were obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you see ranks?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, out of fear, I couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Mahmutovic, did you see the insignia of the Viteska Brigade on any of the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but there were at least two persons who had different uniforms which HVO soldiers did not wear. But the soldier who, according to my personal conviction, was the leader, he wore the insignia of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: HVO insignia?

utterances.speaker: NUSRETA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm trying, but we just get to the point of the questions which the witness was testifying on the original OTP statement, and I think I will need 45 minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: All right. You've had nearly 45 minutes already, Mr. Kovacic. What else have you got to ask about?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I will certainly ask about the second meeting with Cerkez at the UNPROFOR base.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. That's a matter --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And I will also ask about people the witness mentioned. If you have the previous statement of the witness, on the top of page 4, she's mentioning some people here, and I would like to identify those people or to see whether it is possible that those people were there, including a person which was mentioned as one for exchange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, we will adjourn until tomorrow. You've got a quarter of an hour tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I will try to organise my best. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mrs. Mahmutovic, I'm afraid we're not going to finish your evidence today, so we must ask you to come back tomorrow to conclude it. Would you please remember, during the adjournment, not to speak to anybody about your evidence, and that does include members of the Prosecution. So could you be back, please, at half past 2.00 tomorrow, and I hope that we shall be able to finish your evidence fairly soon and then you'll be able to go home. Half past 2.00 tomorrow, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: 5.19 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 7th day of July, 1999, at 2:30 p.m.
